random_seed: single fixed master seed 20260611 (numpy default_rng); 120 trials per condition per sample size

outputs.metric: scan[n=300].subcrit_FPR (false-positive rate of the validated power-law + crackling pipeline on a matched subcritical m=0.9 control at a literature-typical sample size)
outputs.tolerance: Wilson 95% CI [0.325, 0.498]; rejection threshold for the thesis is FPR >= 0.20

outputs.metric: scan[n=300].crit_TPR (true-positive rate on the critical m=1.0 positive control at the same sample size)
outputs.tolerance: Wilson 95% CI [0.738, 0.876]; positive control must pass for a valid (non-DRAW) outcome

outputs.metric: scan[n=2500].subcrit_FPR (FPR only falls below the 0.05 diagnostic target outside the literature-typical regime)
scan[n=4000].crit_TPR (TPR begins to erode as fit_xmin trims short avalanches at large n)

known_limitations: Synthetic Galton-Watson branching process, not real neural recordings. The subcritical control is one specific matched surrogate (Poisson offspring, m=0.9); a single fixed avalanche-detection and fitting pipeline is used. The result establishes that ONE standard, carefully validated power-law + crackling pipeline has a high false-positive rate (~0.30-0.47) on a matched subcritical control at literature-typical sample sizes (n_aval ~ 300-800), and that this rate only falls below the 0.05 diagnostic target at n_aval >= 2500. It does NOT decide whether real cortical dynamics are critical, nor that every literature pipeline behaves identically; more elaborate detection schemes (multi-channel binning, model comparison against explicit alternatives) were not tested. At very large n the positive-control TPR itself begins to erode because the KS-minimised x_min trims short avalanches that are intrinsic to the critical distribution — a separate finite-size/estimator tension, not part of the headline FPR claim.
